newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Blues will be desperate, says Bok lock.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Blues will be desperate, says Bok lock.

text.p: AUCKLAND, April 18 - Gauteng Lions captain and Springboks lock Kobus Wiese says the Auckland Blues will need no more motivation in Saturday's Super 12 rugby match at Eden Park than the fact that they have never beaten his team.
Formerly Transvaal, the Gauteng Lions have arrived in Auckland geared up to play a game of test proportions against the defending champions.
"This is going to be as tough as any Super 12 game. I know there are no easy Super 12 games, but we're expecting a fierce encounter on Saturday," Wiese told NZPA.
"We do have a proud record of being unbeaten against Auckland but it has been at home. That is a big difference.
"They'll come out very keen to set the record straight, but we're also here to play to the best of our ability and for some success. This is going to be a very tough encounter."
The grim look on the Blues' faces at training last night suggested just as much and coach Graham Henry promised the Gauteng Lions that Auckland would be out to pay them back.
"We've made no bones about being beaten by them the last two times we played them,'' Henry said of the Super 10 final loss two years ago and last year's loss at Johannesburg.
"The players have spoken about it, we've discussed it and we want to play even better than we did against the ACT, we will have to.

"They've got a huge pack, they've got three guys in their tight five who played the last World Cup final and if Ian MacDonald (flanker) had been fit he too would have played in that game while their hooker Chris Rossouw was a reserve for that game.
"They've got the ability to put pressure on us and we're aware of that. It shows the quality of the side we're up against."
Henry is expecting the disappointment of last weekend's 16-16 draw against Northern Transvaal to spur the Lions.
"They were the better team, things didn't happen for them so we're expecting them to be even harder this week," he said.
Wiese predicted a near test match atmosphere, claiming some Super 12 games were tougher than some test matches.
"I've always maintained that all Super 12 games are extremely tough. They're really hard and some of the games are tougher than test rugby," he said.
"It is very fierce out there and very competitive. That is the way it is going to be on Saturday."

Auckland Blues: Shane Howarth, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Mark Carter, Leo Lafaiali'i, Jim Coe, Michael Jones, Craig Dowd, Sean Fitzpatrick, Paul Thomson.
